"He did have a knife. He didn't pull it out. I just wasn't comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away," he said. Jefferies said he then held the man down until police arrived. "I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and he was no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can't leave," he said.

Members of the police stand guard at the crime scene of a vehicle attack on Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in Wangaratta, Australia on Oct 19, 2026 in this screen grab obtained from a video. (Photo: Australian Broadcasting Corporation via Reuters)

Haines, 65, was airlifted to hospital where she underwent surgery overnight. She remains in a critical condition.  Early investigations suggested the driver, identified as a 43-year-old man, performed a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said . Counterterrorism authorities are among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. While police have given no motive for the alleged attack, the involvement of counterterrorism investigators has raised alarm that it could have been an act of political violence, which is rare in Australia. Jefferies, whose shop is next door to Haines' electorate office around three hours' drive northeast of Melbourne, described the former midwife as a "genuine, kind person". Albanese praised Jefferies' intervention, calling him a hero. "At this dark and terrible time, an element of light is the fact that a Good Samaritan, someone rushed to Helen's defence in Wangaratta, put themselves potentially at risk by doing so. And that person is a hero today," Albanese said in an interview with the Nine network's "Today" show.  Jefferies downplayed the praise. "I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I just was a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish sort of way," he said.

Source: Reuters

FAST

(Specifies wording in 2nd bullet point to say to "vendor-driven" instead of "vendor-mandated") By Anastasiia Kozlova Oct 20 : Large US and British companies spend 28 per cent of their software budgets on average to pay for vendor-driven upgrades, migration and licensing changes they would not have actively chosen, adding avoidable costs and operational risks in the race to adopt AI solutions, a survey by software maintenance provider Origina showed on Tuesday. These hard-to-avoid recurring costs and operational disruption were described as a "software tax" in the study that surveyed more than 2,000 companies. "When the alternative to an unwanted upgrade is losing support on systems the business runs on, saying yes is often a rational response," Origina CEO Tomas O'Leary said.

• 95 per cent of respondents said they had paid for a vendor-driven upgrade they expected to worsen outcomes, while 80 per cent said leaving a major software vendor would significantly disrupt their business • 84 per cent said senior engineering staff "always" or "often" devoted time to vendor-driven software changes rather than innovation or business-focused development • 91 per cent said they had retired fully functional hardware in the past three years to comply with vendors' support deadlines, sacrificing 1.65 years of remaining useful life on average • O'Leary said the issue was largely universal and also applied to other regions, with older companies with more entrenched technology stacks facing the biggest challenges • According to the report, the most recent vendor-driven software change resulted in an average annual cost of $12.87 million for the surveyed organizations

FAST

LONDON, Oct 20 : Demand for safe-haven assets is strong as AI jitters hurt tech stocks, the Iran war continues and keeps energy prices elevated, while worries about high government debt loads persist. Yet traditional safe havens have not performed as well as expected this year: Gold sold off after the start of the Iran war as investors ditched top-performing assets given losses elsewhere. Government bonds, once considered one of the world's safest assets, are volatile. Here is a look at how some safe havens currently stack up. 1) LOVE/HATE RELATIONSHIP WITH THE DOLLAR

Breaking with last year's 'sell US' theme, the dollar has rallied since the Iran war started, up 4 per cent since late February. That has reinforced its role as a go-to safe haven at times of global stress. A strong economy, higher rates, and the US's energy-exporter status have helped. But factors that caused traders to question the dollar's long-term safe-haven status, such as a more than $40 trillion debt pile and policy uncertainty, have not dissipated. The dollar is also vulnerable to tech selling as it has benefited from record capital inflows into US shares on optimism over the AI investment boom. The dollar could be nearing the back end of a bull market, Societe Generale chief FX strategist Kit Juckes said. "It hasn't got that much further to go," he noted, but said it was hard to justify a sustained bet against the dollar at present because the "big global story is that the dollar is a petrocurrency and we're in the middle of an energy crisis". 2) EUROPE WOBBLES, BUY SWISSIE One takeaway from France-driven bond turmoil is that the Swiss franc is a haven of choice when Europe wobbles. It is up over 2 per cent so far this month against the euro, poised for its biggest monthly jump since late 2023. "Concerns about France's public finances and election uncertainty in France and Spain have supported the franc," said Georgette Boele, senior FX & oil strategist at ABN Amro. She added that investors were also becoming less keen to use the franc to fund carry trades, preferring not to position against a currency with safe-haven qualities. Swiss rates at 0 per cent make the franc popular in trades where investors borrow in a currency with low rates to invest in higher-yielding assets elsewhere. The AI jitters should also benefit the Swiss franc, analysts said. 3) GERMAN BONDS A RELATIVE WINNER Government bonds' reputation as a safe haven has been battered by fiscal concerns. Borrowing costs from the US to Japan recently hit multi-decade highs. The tech-driven stocks selloff has, however, renewed some demand for bonds. There is another noticeable development. When US and French 10-year bond yields hit 24-year peaks earlier this month, German yields fell as their prices rose. Investors say that is a clear sign that triple-A rated German Bunds stand out as safe havens among major economies. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said Germany would remain the anchor of stability in Europe amid bond turmoil and was "getting fit" after years of stagnation. "Everyone worries about contagion in Europe and whether the Bund just gets dragged along with (French) OATs, (Italian) BTPs, so it's good that the Bund has acted as that European risk-off instrument," said Johnathan Owen, a portfolio manager at TwentyFour Asset Management. 4) DID YOU FORGET SHORT-DATED BONDS? Overall, high debt among major economies will continue to hurt long-dated bonds' safe-haven status, investors said. But short-dated government bonds provide some shelter because they are less sensitive to debt worries. "We really like short-dated bonds," said Rory McPherson, chief market strategist at Wren Sterling. "Because of all the concerns over debts and deficits, we haven't been buying longer-dated bonds." 5) GOLD KEEPS ITS SPARKLE Gold, another traditional safe haven, has had a bumpy ride. After hitting record highs at $5,595 per troy ounce in January, it fell after the Iran war started as investors tapped the precious metal, given losses elsewhere. Gold rallied again in August as inflation fears and concern that the Federal Reserve was not doing enough to contain price pressures returned. It is trading around $4,175. Central bank buying and safe-haven demand support prices above $4,000, analysts say. While high interest rates should limit gold's upside, a tense geopolitical backdrop and US fiscal worries should bolster the safe-haven metal further out. "In the longer term, gold should again benefit from continued strong central-bank buying and renewed concerns over US debt and its rising interest burden," said Julius Baer analyst Carsten Menke.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Indonesia battles to stabilise market after MSCI expulsion threat
item.description: Indonesian stocks rose on Tuesday as authorities in Jakarta introduced measures to restrict selling after a record two-day $82 billion rout sparked by index provider MSCI's warning of possible removal from its global indexes.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Banerjee, Stefanno Sulaiman
item.content:encoded: Indonesian stocks rose on Tuesday as authorities in Jakarta introduced measures to restrict selling after a [USN:L1N46500W TEXT:"record two-day"] $82 billion rout sparked by index provider MSCI's [USN:L4N46509U TEXT:"warning"] of possible [USN:L6N4620Z3 TEXT:"removal"] from its global indexes. Jakarta's benchmark index (.JKSE) advanced 5.3%, after hitting a six-year low in the previous session as the world's worst-performing stock market this year dropped 14.8% over Friday and Monday. The index is down about 40% this year. The selloff was sparked by MSCI's [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"warning"] on Friday that Indonesia could be reclassified as a "[USN:L6N46208E TEXT:"standalone"]" market from "emerging markets", a harsher-than-expected downgrade that stunned investors and policymakers and raised fears of large-scale passive fund outflows. The index provider cited Indonesia's failure to improve ownership transparency and curb coordinated trading, turning what had been a downgrade risk to "frontier" market status into a full-blown crisis of investor confidence. Relegation to "standalone" status would mark a major setback for Southeast Asia's biggest economy as investors grow increasingly uneasy about the country's fiscal health and the autonomy of its central bank under President Prabowo Subianto. Foreign investors have already pulled nearly $5 billion from Indonesian equities this year, with Goldman Sachs estimating a removal by MSCI could spur $5.6 billion of passive outflows. After an online meeting with MSCI on Monday, the Indonesia Stock Exchange said it would exclude from its benchmark index any stocks with a high concentration of ownership by any person or entity. "We are doing what is best for our market," IDX President Director Jeffrey Hendrik said, adding the exclusion would provide a more accurate picture of the index's movements. He said the affected stocks account for roughly 18% of the total index weight. Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, said excluding tightly held stocks should help address some investability concerns, but implementation would be key, given the potential for domestic pushback. "From here, we think the bigger incremental risk to flows is likely to come from active rather than passive funds," he said. EYES ON CENTRAL BANK MSCI's warning has weighed on the rupiah , which strengthened slightly to 17,980 per US dollar on Tuesday but remained close to the record low of 18,190 hit in June ahead of a policy decision from Indonesia's central bank. Bank Indonesia is expected to hold rates steady on Wednesday, although some economists have raised the prospect of a rate hike to defend the currency, which is down 7% this year. George Xu, a director in Fitch Ratings' sovereigns team, said the latest concerns and substantial market selloff reinforced the risks the rating agency identified when it [USN:L1N3ZS06T TEXT:"revised the outlook"] on Indonesia to negative in March. "From sovereign rating perspective, we do not anticipate the consultation announcement itself to have material immediate credit implications," he said, but added that external pressure could raise the government’s borrowing costs and erode external buffers. "PLEASE PRAY," WATCHDOG URGES AMID INVESTOR UNEASE To stem the rout, the stock exchange this week halved the daily down limit on stock prices to 7% from 15%, while setting a 1 rupiah down limit on shares priced at 14 rupiah or less. Market watchers said the move to remove stocks with highly concentrated ownership from the benchmark index was a constructive step, but noted investors would still have some exposure to those firms through direct ownership and investment products such as mutual funds. "We must ensure that even if a stock is delisted from the Jakarta Composite Index, concentration risk does not continue to accumulate within products purchased by the public," said Liza Camelia Suryanata, head of research at stockbroker Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia. Also on Monday, Prabowo held talks with finance chiefs, including the head of the Financial Services Authority (OJK), the finance minister and the BI governor. After the meeting, OJK chief Friderica Widyasari Dewi said the regulator would continue to advance Indonesia's capital market reforms, particularly regarding transparency, liquidity, and law enforcement against various forms of violations. "The stock market has started to rebound today; the important thing is to keep building confidence," said OJK's Friderica in a separate event. "I haven't had a moment's rest since Friday. Please pray that we can get through this successfully."

item.title: Infantino set to visit Japan to seek Asian backing for FIFA re-election bid
item.description: The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Sports / Football News / Infantino set to visit Japan to seek Asian backing for FIFA re-election bid

Infantino set to visit Japan to seek Asian backing for FIFA re-election bid The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded

Gianni Infantino, president of FIFA | Image: Bloomberg

AP Tokyo 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 4:01 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Gianni Infantino's campaign for re-election as FIFA president is set to move this week to Japan and a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with the Asian Football Confederation. This comes after Infantino apologized last week in Zurich, Switzerland, to FIFA's 37-member ruling council - which he chairs - for "mistakes" he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2 billion sell-off plan for the World Cup. The council is the main decision-making body at FIFA with a global spread of officials. The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the president of the AFC, expressed early opposition to Infantino and his plan to create a subsidiary to run the World Cup, but may have moved closer to Infantino, The Athletic has reported.

Also Read

FIFA chief Infantino apologises for World Cup row, fails to appease critics

FIFA plans to double development funding; India could receive $25 million

UEFA sets criteria for candidate to challenge Infantino and overhaul FIFA

FIFA leadership battle looms as European football chiefs discuss Infantino

Saudi Arabia shelves $2.5 billion Neom Stadium plan for 2034 World Cup

Infantino has offered to critics an open, independent review of how FIFA makes its decisions. Infantino is electioneering   An Associated Press tally indicates Infantino is close to landing the simple majority of the 211 FIFA member federations he needs to win re-election in March to a fourth term. Some of the deciding votes could some from Asia. The AFC had joined the criticism of Infantino in the wake of the proposed World Cup sell-off, but its members appear far from united. Qatar, the 2022 World Cup host, has expressed support for the FIFA leader while Jordan has declared its opposition. The FIFA Council is scheduled to meet next on Dec. 16 in Doha, Qatar.

The Associated Press count shows 87 of the 211 FIFA Member federations have indicated support for Infantino either in individual comments or by endorsing statements of support by their regional confederations. The largest block of opposition comes from Europe. The FIFA voting system   No sitting FIFA president has lost an election since 1974. The deadline for a candidate to file against Infantino is Nov. 18. FIFA rules state candidates must have "played an active role in association football (e.g. as a player or an official within FIFA, a confederation or an association, etc.) for two of the last five years before being proposed." They must have "declarations of support" from at least five of the 211 members. "FIFA is a massive patronage network," Jules Boykoff, a political scientist at Pacific University and a former professional soccer player, told The Associated Press. "It brings in billions from the men's World Cup and distributes it to football associations around the world in exchange for loyalty."   "The funds that FIFA distributes to soccer bodies around the world are meant to develop soccer, but there's scant oversight," Boykoff added. "To say FIFA is in need of structural overhaul it to make an enormous understatement.

item.title: PNB cautions customers of AI-led cyberattacks amid cyber fraud surge
item.description: bank informed customers that fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated methods to make their attempts more convincing ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Banking / PNB cautions customers of AI-led cyberattacks amid cyber fraud surge

PNB cautions customers of AI-led cyberattacks amid cyber fraud surge Bank informed customers that fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated methods to make their attempts more convincing

| Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 4:00 PM IST

Listen to This Article

State-run Punjab National Bank (PNB) has cautioned its customers about AI-enabled cyberattacks, especially AI voice cloning, deepfakes, and phishing, amid surging incidents of fraud, and has advised them to remain vigilant. Highlighting that October is observed as National Cyber Security Awareness Month every year, the bank informed customers that fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated methods to make their attempts more convincing. "Many cyber frauds today exploit human behaviour, particularly trust, fear, urgency and everyday digital habits. Fraudsters may imitate the voice or appearance of your family members, friends, or trusted persons and create a false emergency to seek an urgent transfer of money," PNB MD and CEO Ashok Chandra said in his message to customers.   Similarly, fraudulent emails, SMS or messages may appear highly personalised and like genuine bank communications, making them more difficult to identify, he said, adding that they create panic and make customers act without verification. In view of rising incidents of cybercrimes across the country, the domestic public and private sector banks are actively ramping up IT and cybersecurity investments to combat evolving threats from advanced artificial intelligence, quantum computing risks, and strict regulatory mandates from the Reserve Bank of India. Also Read

Nifty PSU Bank index surges 3%; PNB, PSB, Canara, Union Bank soar up to 8%

PNB's foreign bank MoU 10-15 days away, says MD & CEO Ashok Chandra premium

Punjab National Bank Q2 results: Net profit rises 13% to ₹5,532 crore

PM Modi calls for global framework to tackle cyber fraud, deepfakes

Axis, AU Bank, PNB: Brokerages identify 5 bank stocks after RBI hikes rate

Pointing out that all these scams run on the fuel called urgency, 63SATS Cybertech Joint MD & Joint CEO Srinivas L said, "A cloned voice of a son saying he has been arrested. A video of a police officer threatening a digital arrest. A message saying the bank account will be blocked in an hour. The technology has changed, but the playbook has not. It makes people panic, which pressurises them to pay."   So, the counter is simple, Srinivas said, adding there is an urgent need to pause, verify on a channel one chooses, hang up, and call the person back on the number saved in the phone. Agree on a family code word that only your household knows, because AI can copy a voice, but it cannot copy a secret, he added. Srinivas further said that maintaining digital hygiene is the need of the hour for people around the globe to save themselves from emerging cyber frauds. "People should turn on two-factor authentication for email, banking and social media, and use a different password for each. They must set a daily limit on UPI and card transactions so a single mistake cannot empty their accounts,'' he added. Reaffirming its commitment to safeguarding the hard-earned money and personal information of customers, PNB's Chandra said awareness and vigilance remain the strongest partners in preventing cyber frauds. ''Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility. Your awareness combined with our security measures creates the strongest defence against cyber frauds,'' he added.

item.description: Stellantis India has a long-standing partnership with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle for manufacturing through a joint venture ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Auto / Stellantis India aims to halve vehicle development time, boost localisation

Stellantis India aims to halve vehicle development time, boost localisation Stellantis India has a long-standing partnership with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle for manufacturing through a joint venture

Stellantis has one of its software and technology centre in Bengaluru (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 3:59 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Stellantis India is targeting to halve vehicle development time and ramp up localisation for certain models as it prepares to launch 12 products across Citroen and Jeep brands under its FaSTLAne 2030 roadmap, MD and CEO Shailesh Hazela said. "Globally, we announced that our ambition is to cut down our development time for bringing new products from 48 months to close to two years, which is around 24 months. That is what we are working on (for) our products, which we are going to launch," Hazela told PTI in an interview. Stellantis has one of its software and technology centre in Bengaluru.   "[Our] India engineering centre is part of the four large tech centres in the world. We have the largest tech centre and they develop cars not only for Jeep and Citroen, but for models globally. So they have the same mandate [cut in product development time] which they will be following," he said. Also, Stellantis India has a long-standing partnership with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle for manufacturing through a joint venture. Recently, they signed a definitive agreement to expand the scope of their partnership into advanced technology and product collaboration. Also Read

India's auto tech funding at $1.3 bn in 2026, unlikely to match 2025 levels premium

Auto tech cos raise $1.3 bn across 97 funding rounds in 2026 so far: Tracxn

BS-VII clock starts ticking as Centre sets 2029 target for emission norms

European carmakers to favour India as it emerges as global hub: Goyal

Both the companies plan to jointly develop vehicles for more than 50 global markets and manufacture them in India at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited, the 50:50 joint venture between Tata Motors and Stellantis. On localisation, Hazela said Citroen has localisation level in the range of 90-95 per cent, while Jeep brand's localisation stands at around 70-75 per cent. "We are working on a foundation which is local engineering and local supply chain to get localisation of 90 per cent plus in our products here. That gives us flexibility to be in the pricing range that the market expects," he said. Meanwhile, Stellantis India has announced an investment of Rs 4,000 crore over the next three years as it prepares to launch 12 models, including seven new, across Citroen and Jeep brands. The investment will be mainly in products, localisation for customer experience. Jeep brand currently has four models in India - Compass, Wrangler, Meridian and Grand Cherokee, while Citroen also has four models -- C3, BasaltX, AircrossX, C5 Aircross. Of the new products planned, Jeep brand will get four new models -- one SUV each in B, C and D segments, along with a D segment pickup. Citroen will get three new models -- one C segment SUV, D segment MPV and one A segment car.

item.content:encoded:
午前のドル158円半ば、レンジ上限で動けず　円の弱さ指摘も 12:28 配信

米ドル紙幣。26年3月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Atsuko Aoyama

[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 午前のドルは１５８円半ばでの膠着が続いた。直近のレンジ上限に当たり、上抜けるにも押し下げるにも材料に乏しいとの声がある。上値では日米の協調為替介入への警戒でドル買い／円売りに追随する動きは強まっていないが、他資産に比べた円の弱さが改めて意識されているとの見方も聞かれた。

・ドル／円、午前中は１５８円半ばで膠着

・直近のレンジの上限、２００日移動平均線近辺で上値重い

・来週以降のイベント待ちで動けずとの声も

・前日のドル／円はレンジ上抜け試す動き、円の弱さ浮き彫りとの声

・一部に高市早苗首相の財源巡るⅩ投稿を円売り材料視する向きも

・ドル１５９円台では円安けん制など口先介入に警戒

＜トレイダーズ証券の井口喜雄・市場部長＞

「ドル／円は直近のレンジ上限で２００日移動平均線近辺にあるが、ブレイクするようなイベントがない。じりじりとして動きが少なく、例えばレンジ上限で売るという判断も躊躇するところ」

「米国のＩＴ株が振るわない中でドルを買う理由にも乏しい。一方、市場が深刻なリスクオフとなった場合は円キャリーが剥がれてドル安／円高が進むかもれないが、今のような株の調整程度なら動意づくこともない」

「円買い理由があるとすれば日銀の利上げ加速だが、それが見えない。来年３－４月までの米国の利上げ観測を踏まえると金利差は一向に縮まらず、ドル／円を下目線ではみられない」

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
午前の日経平均は続落、ＡＩ株の一角に売り継続　下げ渋りも 11:59 配信

写真は2026年4月、東京証券取引所内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Hiroko Hamada

[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は続落し、前営業日比０．６２％（４０４円３５銭）安の６万４５１２円３５銭となった。人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを手がける米コアウィーブを巡る懸念がくすぶる中、引き続きＡＩ関連株の一角が安く、日経平均は軟調な展開となった。原油価格の高止まりや米金利高も投資家心理の重しとなった。日経平均は一時１％超安となったが、一部半導体株に買い戻しも入り、終盤は下げ渋った。

・日経平均は前営業日比０．２５％安でスタートした後、一時１．５７％（１０２２円）安の６万３８９４円６７銭まで下落。

・寄与度の大きいＡＩ・半導体関連株の下げが強まった。韓国株安も重し。個別ではソフトバンクグループ、フジクラが大幅下落。

・売りが一巡した後は一部半導体株がプラスに転じ、日経平均は下げ幅を縮小。終盤にかけては６万４５００円台でもみ合い。

・物色面では銀行株が軟調。決算を手掛かりにした売買も。

・ＴＯＰＩＸは０．８８％安の４０３１．８５ポイントで午前の取引を終了。東証プライム市場の売買代金は３兆０８２１億６８００万円。

・東証３３業種では、鉄鋼、その他製品、精密機器など５業種が値上がり。非鉄金属、銀行、海運など２８業種が値下がり。

・東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが２５６銘柄（１６％）、値下がりは１２５４銘柄（８０％）、変わらずは４１銘柄（２％）。

＜いちよし証券　投資情報部　銘柄情報課課長　及川敬司氏＞

「米コアウィーブのような新興企業の資金繰り懸念がくすぶっているが、半導体製造装置や素材関連株がいっしょくたに売られているのは違和感もある。これから本格化する決算で好業績が確認されれば、（半導体関連株に）買い戻しが入る可能性もある」

「目先は金融政策会合や米中間選挙などイベントを控え、動きづらくなりそうだが、イベント通過後は再び上方向を試す展開を想定」

item.title: Gavin McKenna, 18, nets winning goal as Maple Leafs top Sharks
item.description: Rookie Gavin McKenna netted the game-winning goal as the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the San Jose Sharks 3-1 on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie Gavin McKenna netted the game-winning goal as the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the San Jose Sharks 3-1 on Monday night. McKenna gave the Maple Leafs a 2-1 lead 4:56 into the final frame, receiving the puck from Auston Matthews on the outside and enjoying a relatively unimpeded path toward goal. The 18-year-old was allowed to stroll forward and ping it in off the post for his first NHL power-play goal in his 10th game. The game marked the first encounter between McKenna and Ivar Stenberg, the highly touted top two picks of the 2026 NHL Draft. McKenna was selected first overall out of Penn State, just ahead of Stenberg, who previously played in his native Sweden. Mason Marchment scored in the first period for San Jose before Matthews tied the game with 12 seconds remaining in the second period. Matthews added two assists for his fourth multi-point game of the young season. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 30 shots in his first home win as a Maple Leaf. Yaroslav Askarov made 29 saves for the visitors. Toronto snapped a three-game losing streak (0-2-1), while San Jose fell to 1-3-1 in its past five games. Marchment opened the scoring 13:54 in. Tyler Toffoli snatched up Toronto's clearing attempt at the point and flipped the puck to Marchment lurking behind the play. The former Maple Leaf pulled the puck out of the air and shoveled it over a sprawling Bobrovsky. The Sharks were able to kill off a 58-second five-on-three toward the end of the first period after Jacob Trouba and Dmitry Orlov were called for consecutive tripping penalties. Matthews tied the game 1-1 at the end of the second period on what was Toronto's fourth power play. Kirill Marchenko spun away from Trouba in the corner and slipped the puck to the captain, who ripped in a powerful one-timer from one knee. Macklin Celebrini was responsible for the penalty after jumping onto the ice too early, resulting in a too-many-men call. Nick Paul sealed the deal on an empty-net goal with less than 40 seconds remaining from just inside the offensive zone. The Sharks are one of two teams still without a regulation win on the season. --Field Level Media

item.description:
Wen-Yee Lee
[台北 ２０日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手マイクロン・テクノロジーの台湾・桃園拠点で働く従...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米マイクロンの台湾・桃園労組、22日にスト開始　賞与巡り対立 11:56 配信

写真はマイクロン・テクノロジーの看板。2026年9月、台湾桃園市で撮影。REUTERS/Ann Wang

Wen-Yee Lee

[台北 ２０日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手マイクロン・テクノロジーの台湾・桃園拠点で働く従業員を代表する労働組合は、２２日にストライキを開始すると発表した。同社と、台中拠点の従業員を代表する別の労組との間で行われる交渉に合わせて行われるもので、賞与を巡る対立が激化している。

マイクロンにとって、人工知能（ＡＩ）サーバーの主要部品であるＤＲＡＭや広帯域メモリー（ＨＢＭ）を生産する最も重要な製造拠点の一つ。

桃園の労組はストについて、台中の労組との連帯を示すとともに、マイクロンに対し具体的な利益配分案を提示するよう圧力を強めることを目的としていると述べた。

マイクロンは台湾で約１万５０００人を雇用しており、桃園と台中の各事業部門の労働者を代表する別々の労組が存在する。

マイクロンと桃園労組との間の交渉は９月、合意に至らずに終了。同労組は１０月上旬、組合員からスト実施の承認を得た。

台湾で最大規模のマイクロン拠点の従業員を代表する台中労組は、現在も同社と交渉を続けている。同労組は、スト実施の是非に関する投票をまだ行っていない。

桃園労組はスト期間については明らかにしておらず、２２日に詳細を発表するとしている。

台湾の頼清徳総統は先週、労使双方に誠実な交渉を呼びかけた。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州ＥＶ登録、9月は前年比70.3％増　シェア30％超 11:50 配信

写真は小鵬汽車のEV「G9L」。2026年10月12日、パリモーターショーで撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

[１９日 ロイター] - ９月の欧州バッテリー式電気自動車（ＢＥＶ）登録台数は前年同月比７０．３％増加した。原油高や補助金、手頃な価格の車種拡充が引き続き伸びをけん引した。

Ｅモビリティー・ヨーロッパ、ニュー・オートモーティブ、フィア・オートモーティブが１９日公表したデータによると、フランスとドイツが欧州連合（ＥＵ）の自動車排ガス規制案の緩和で合意する中、欧州主要１７市場で９月に販売された自動車の約３分の１をＢＥＶが占めた。

・９月のＢＥＶ登録台数は３０万０２０２台、市場シェアは３２．６％となった。

・欧州における年初来の累計登録台数は１９８万台で、２０２５年の同期間から３８．１％増加した。

・国別では、フランスが６万５２４３台で市場シェアは４１．７％、ドイツは８万８７２４台で、シェアは３４．６％となった。

・北欧は引き続き欧州で電動化が最も進んだ市場となった。ＢＥＶの市場シェアはノルウェーが９８．８％で首位、次いでデンマークの８８．８％、フィンランドの６２．７％、スウェーデンの４９．０％となった。

・アイルランド、ポルトガル、ベルギー、オランダでは、登録台数の約半数をＢＥＶが占めた。

・チェコ、イタリア、ポーランドは引き続き欧州で最も電動化が遅れている市場に入り、ＢＥＶのシェアはそれぞれ１１．２％、７．６％、６．２％だった。

item.title: Australian barber hailed as hero for running to lawmaker's rescue during attack
item.description: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies has been hailed as a hero for running out of his store to detain a man who authorities allege deliberately drove a car into lawmaker Helen Haines in the small town of Wangaratta, an incident that has shocked the country.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chen
item.content:encoded: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies has been hailed as a hero for running out of his store to detain a man who authorities allege deliberately drove a car into lawmaker Helen Haines in the small town of Wangaratta, an incident that has shocked the country. Jefferies had just finished haircuts for a young family on Monday when he said he heard a "loud bang" outside his shop and realised the driver of a Toyota LandCruiser had [USN:L1N46508R TEXT:"struck Haines, "]leaving her badly injured. "It was crazy, I just ran out the front to see what was happening," he told reporters on Tuesday. He said he ran to assist the well-respected local MP, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car. "He did have a knife. He didn't pull it out. I just wasn't comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away," he said. Jefferies said he then held the man down until police arrived. "I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and he was no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can't leave," he said. Haines, 65, was airlifted to hospital where she underwent surgery overnight. She [USN:L1N46510F TEXT:"remains in a critical condition"]. Early investigations suggested the driver, identified as a 43-year-old man, performed a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. Counterterrorism authorities are among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. While police have given no motive for the alleged attack, the involvement of counterterrorism investigators has raised alarm that it could have been an act of political violence, which is rare in Australia. Jefferies, whose shop is next door to Haines' electorate office around three hours' drive northeast of Melbourne, described the former midwife as a "genuine, kind person". Albanese praised Jefferies' intervention, calling him a hero. "At this dark and terrible time, an element of light is the fact that a Good Samaritan, someone rushed to Helen's defence in Wangaratta, put themselves potentially at risk by doing so. And that person is a hero today," Albanese said in an interview with the Nine network's "Today" show. Jefferies downplayed the praise. "I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I just was a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish sort of way," he said.

写真はオープンＡＩのロゴ。2026年6月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Echo Wang　Krystal Hu　Sabrina Valle

[ニューヨーク １９日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業オープンＡＩは、競合アンソロピックが１１月中旬に予定している上場に先立ち、投資家からのコミットメントを確保するために急ピッチで動いている。関係筋２人が明らかにした。オープンＡＩの企業価値は１兆４０００億ドルを超えるとみられているという。

同筋によると、オープンＡＩは似たような投資家層を取り込んでいるアンソロピックに先んじたいという意向を持っているほか、新モデルのリリースを受けた最近の収益成長を生かしたいと考えている。

同筋の１人は、ソフトバンクグループ、アブダビに拠点を置くＭＧＸ、オープンＡＩのその他の既存出資者が約３００億ドル規模の資金調達ラウンドへの参加について協議していると明らかにした。

オープンＡＩは先週、ロングオンリーファンドや政府系ファンドと面会。一方、アンソロピックは独自のインベスター・デーを開催していた。関係筋によると、オープンＡＩの資金調達ラウンドは、この規模の案件としては異例なほど迅速に進む見通し。

同社に詳しい投資家によると、新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）市場の悪化により２０２７年に予定されている上場がさらに遅れる場合、オープンＡＩは巨額のインフラ投資を賄い、バランスシートを強化するためにも資金が必要だという。

オープンＡＩ、ソフトバンクＧはコメントを控えた。アンソロピックとＭＧＸはコメント要請に応じていない。

Shares slide again as oil stays high; AI earnings in focus

People walk under electronic screens displaying Japan's Nikkei share average, at a conference hall in Tokyo, Japan, August 19, 2026. REUTERS/Manami Yamada

FAST

Oct 20 : European shares fell for the second straight day on Tuesday, as another rise in crude oil prices kept risk sentiment in check, while investor focus honed in on results from key AI bellwether companies later this week.  The pan-European STOXX 600 dipped 0.6 per cent after dropping close to 1 per cent on Monday, with European semiconductor companies including ASML and ASMI falling more than 3 per cent.  The euro recouped some losses from the previous day, while yields on French government bonds edged lower after their biggest one-day jump in about a month, as widespread protests underscored difficulties the government faces in reducing its large deficit. France's cities were calm overnight under curfews imposed after last weekend's scenes of chaos, as protest groups announced a new round of demonstrations next Saturday.

"The weekend's protests have further intensified concerns about French public finances given the size of the austerity measures needed to significantly reduce the budget deficit," said Pia Fromlet, an economist at SEB. French stocks, however, showed no signs of respite and fell in line with the broader market weakness.  Crude prices resumed their climb, with Brent hitting a five-month high above $110 a barrel. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they launched several attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, fell 0.2 per cent to 101.77. The euro was up 0.2 per cent at $1.122.  The Japanese yen strengthened 0.2 per cent after an auction of long-dated Japanese government bonds drew record demand. Meanwhile, media reports said the Bank of Japan may raise its inflation outlook for the next fiscal year in forecasts due this month.  In the US, futures on the tech-heavy Nasdaq slipped 0.3 per cent a day after technology stocks found some footing following last week's sharp selloff. EARNINGS AND AI MAJORS IN FOCUS The spotlight is on corporate earnings. Investors will be looking for evidence that consumers and the broader economy remain resilient, but chiefly, that the vast amount of capital pouring into the AI buildout is showing signs of paying off. Reflecting some of this nervousness was a near-30 per cent drop in shares of South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group on Tuesday, when the stock fell below its initial public offering price in its market debut. Quarterly earnings are due from SpaceX and Netflix on Tuesday, with results from AI heavyweights such as Meta and Tesla scheduled for later in the week. "Investors are fine with AI being used more. What they're questioning is whether every dollar of AI capex earns more than it costs to finance," said Ninghui Liu, head of investment strategy and research for APAC at State Street Investment Management. With oil prices around five-month highs, gold remained under a touch of pressure, down 0.4 per cent at $4,122 an ounce, while in cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 0.7 per cent to $81,339.5, and ether eased 0.6 per cent to $2,383.4. Elsewhere, the Canadian dollar rose against the US dollar, which fell 0.35 per cent to C$1.406, after residents in Alberta voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation. Finally, a number of European Central Bank officials, including Martin Kocher and Olli Rehn, speak on Tuesday, as well as Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee member Megan Greene. Their words may help shape investors' expectations for interest rates in the euro zone and Britain.

Source: Reuters

item.description: [フランクフルト １９日 ロイター] - スイス製薬大手ロシュは、ドイツの医療費削減政策に関連して今後の同国への投資を...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ロシュ、今後のドイツ向け投資を全面保留　医療費削減提案で 11:10 配信

写真はロシュのロゴ。2020年1月、スイス・バーゼルで撮影。REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann

[フランクフルト １９日 ロイター] - スイス製薬大手ロシュは、ドイツの医療費削減政策に関連して今後の同国への投資を全面的に見直している。ドイツ医薬品事業の責任者ダニエル・シュタイナーズ氏が１９日、ウェルト紙のインタビューで明らかにした。

シュタイナーズ氏は「ドイツにおける今後の投資決定を当面全て保留にしている」と述べ、政策立案者らが最近、製薬業界に対し「多くの信頼を損ねた」と付け加えた。

• ドイツ連邦保健省報道官は「ドイツを事業拠点としないとの企業の決定は遺憾で、わが国と欧州連合（ＥＵ）がこれらの課題を真剣に受け止めなければならないことを示している」と語った。

• 同省は欧州レベルでの交渉を含め、ドイツおよび欧州における製薬業界のための安定的かつ魅力的な枠組み条件の整備を提唱していくという。

• シュタイナーズ氏は、政策立案者らが法定健康保険制度の構造的な問題に取り組む代わりに短期的な経費節減に注力し、業界にさらなる負担を強いていると指摘した。

• 同氏は、研究・生産に従事する製薬企業の製造業者割引に関する負担軽減を目的とした立地条項の提案は、この法律による悪影響を部分的にしか相殺できないとし、必要なのは包括的な戦略だと強調。ドイツ政府は立地条件に関する提案を検討中で、検討の結果については現時点で予断を許さないという。

• ドイツで法定健康保険制度の急増する費用に上限を設ける法案が提案されたことを受け、米製薬大手イーライリリー は既に６月に同国への計画投資額２３億ユーロ（２５億７０００万ドル）を半減すると表明している。

Malaysia has made no commitment to provide financing support to AirAsia, ministry says

Any request for support from companies in any sector "will be considered based on the interests of the country and the people, the fiscal sustainability of the government and the protection of public funds", said Malaysia's finance ministry.

AirAsia planes on the tarmac at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2). (File Photo: Reuters//Najjua Zulkefli)

FAST

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial assistance to budget airline operator AirAsia , the finance ministry said, though it acknowledged concerns over the carrier's financial health following a jump in jet fuel prices. Reuters reported this month, citing sources, that AirAsia was in talks with the government over potential support. The airline's co-founder Tony Fernandes said the talks focused on aviation-related costs such as airport charges and fuel, not financial assistance In a written parliamentary reply on Monday (Oct 19), the finance ministry said it was monitoring developments in Malaysia's aviation sector, including recent quarterly losses reported by AirAsia that were attributed to rising fuel costs stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran. The government was regularly engaging with aviation players and seeking views from industry and technical experts, as was the case for other economic sectors affected by the Middle East crisis, it said.

Any request for support from companies in any sector "will be considered based on the interests of the country and the people, the fiscal sustainability of the government and the protection of public funds, in accordance with applicable laws and procedures", the ministry said. "To date, the government has not made any agreement or commitment to provide financing support to AirAsia, whether in the form of guarantees, loans or public fund injections," it said.

Related:

Despite AirAsia chief’s rebuttal, analysts less sanguine over budget carrier’s financial plight

Timeline: From budget-airline pioneer to financial strain - how did AirAsia get here?

The ministry said AirAsia was a significant player in the aviation sector, accounting for around 41 per cent of the 104.5 million passenger movements recorded at airports operated by Malaysia Airports Holdings in 2025 and almost 60 per cent of domestic passenger movements. The carrier also played a significant role in maintaining air connectivity in Malaysia's Sabah and Sarawak states on Borneo island, it said.

相次ぐサイバー攻撃、金融機関にも「適切かつ迅速な対応促す」＝片山金融相 10:45 配信

写真は片山さつき金融担当相。8月3日、東京で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Takaya Yamaguchi

［東京　２０日　ロイター］ - 片山さつき金融担当相は２０日、日本企業へのサイバー攻撃が相次ぐ現状を踏まえ、金融機関に対しても適切な対応を促す考えを示した。同日午前の閣議後会見で語った。

サイバー攻撃を巡り、金融機関には１０月９日に注意喚起を出していた。ただ、金融機関の委託先への不正アクセスを通じて個人情報が流出する事例もあり、片山金融相は「委託先などのリスク管理を含むサイバーセキュリティ対策も求めた」と述べた。

金融システムへの影響を未然に防ぐため、「サイバー攻撃の動向も踏まえながら、金融機関に対して適切かつ迅速な対応を促していく」としている。

item.title: Mobile wallet operator GCash parent Mynt ends flat after record Philippine IPO
item.description: Fintech firm Mynt , operator of mobile wallet GCash, ended flat on its first day of trade market after raising around $967 million in the largest-ever IPO in the Philippines, marking a steadier debut than recent regional technology listings.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Karen Lema, Roshan Thomas
item.content:encoded: Fintech firm Mynt (GCASH.PS) , operator of mobile wallet GCash, ended flat on its first day of trade market after raising around $967 million in the largest-ever IPO in the Philippines, marking a steadier debut than recent regional technology listings. The stock opened at 6.60 pesos per share, in line with its offer price, and rose as much as 2.4% to 6.76 pesos before closing at 6.60 pesos. The closing price valued Mynt at about 442 billion pesos ($7 billion), making it one of the country's largest listed companies. "Mynt's flat debut is a plausible outcome given the development of regional listings," said Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based Shenton Research. "Issuers have to balance valuation against getting the money raised to get the deal done." Mynt's IPO and market debut comes amid a recent [USN:L1N46605X TEXT:"broader selloff"] in AI-related shares globally, which saw some IPOs getting pulled or [USN:FWN4660V7 TEXT:"delayed"], and investors becoming more selective. Firmus [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"pulled its Australian IPO"], while AirTrunk [USN:L4N45Z0H4 TEXT:"delayed its planned Singapore REIT listing"]. South Korean AI firm Elice [USN:L1N46600F TEXT:"fell sharply on its debut"], while [USN:L1N45V02W TEXT:"Eswin"] and [USN:L1N461058 TEXT:"Transsion"], which listed in Hong Kong this month, closed below their offer prices on their first day of trade. Mynt's IPO, which raised 60.9 billion pesos after including an overallotment option, surpassed Monde Nissin's (MONDE.PS) 52.2-billion-peso IPO in 2021 to become the Philippines biggest-ever IPO, according to LSEG data. In a Tuesday [USN:FWN4660UZ TEXT:"stock exchange filing"], stabilising agent UBS said it may purchase up to 1.204 billion overallotment shares in the open market during the stabilisation period, which ends no more than 30 days from the listing date. Global investors including BlackRock, Citadel and Fidelity International bought Mynt shares in the IPO, in what analysts say, would be a boost for a Southeast Asian market, which has struggled to attract foreign investments. The Philippine stock market index is down 4.08% so far this year, and foreign investors sold 20.86 billion pesos worth of shares from January to August, a PSE monthly report showed . Mynt President and CEO Martha Sazon said the listing marked a new stage in the company's effort to broaden access to financial services for Filipinos who have long been outside the formal banking system. Nearly 90% of GCash customers come from low- to middle-income households, she said. BIGGEST IN THE PHILIPPINES Mynt, backed by Globe Telecom (GLO.PS) , Ant Group and Ayala Corp (AC.PS) , owns GCash, the Philippines' largest finance app, according to its prospectus. The platform offers payments, money transfers, lending, savings, investments and insurance products. The domestic market-focused company had 41.5 million monthly active users in the three-month period that ended on June 30, or nearly 56% of the Philippines' adult population, according to its IPO prospectus. GCash users completed payment transactions worth 9.84 trillion pesos in the first half of 2026. "It is a record and, more importantly, a statement of confidence in Mynt, in the Philippine economy and in the strength of our capital market," Philippine Stock Exchange President and CEO Ramon Monzon said. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the listing came at a time when the stock market needed renewed investor interest and broader participation, adding that attracting fresh capital remained a challenge. He said strong demand from local and international investors offered a "reason for optimism" and reflected continued confidence in Filipino enterprises. Mynt sold 8.03 billion shares at 6.60 pesos each. Mynt plans to use the proceeds to fund growth in its digital financial services business, product development and general corporate purposes, according to its prospectus. Mynt said that for the six months ending June 30, its net income rose 7.3% from a year earlier to 10.82 billion pesos. Revenue rose 10.4% to 43.27 billion pesos. Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan and UBS acted as joint global coordinators and joint bookrunners for the IPO, while Jefferies, CLSA and HSBC were international joint bookrunners. Mynt, the operator of mobile wallet GCash, raised about US$966.99 million after selling over 8 billion shares.

Traders work on the trading floor of the Philippine Stock Exchange, in Taguig City, Metro Manila, Philippines. (File photo: Reuters/Eloisa Lopez)

FAST

MANILA: Shares of fintech firm Mynt, operator of mobile wallet GCash, rose 1.7 per cent in its market debut on Tuesday (Oct 20) after the company raised 60.9 billion pesos (US$966.99 million) in the largest initial public offering on record in the Philippines. The stock opened at 6.60 pesos a share, in line with its offer price, before rising to 6.71 pesos. The broader Philippine Stock Exchange index was down 0.02 per cent. The firm's debut demonstrated investor demand for Mynt's payments business even as a broader sell-off in AI-related shares made investors more selective about new tech listings. "It is a record and, more importantly, a statement of confidence in Mynt, in the Philippine economy and in the strength of our capital market," Philippine Stock Exchange president and CEO Ramon Monzon said.

Mynt's listing came as South Korean AI firm Elice fell sharply in its market debut on Tuesday, highlighting a more cautious mood toward companies tied to the AI boom. Mynt president and CEO Martha Sazon said the listing marked a new stage in the company's effort to widen access to financial services for Filipinos who have long been outside the formal banking system. Nearly 90 per cent of GCash customers come from low- to middle-income households, she said.

Related:

CNA Explains: Why are AI stocks tumbling when demand is still booming?

Mynt, backed by Globe Telecom, Ant Group and Ayala Corp, owns GCash, the Philippines' largest finance app, according to its prospectus. The platform offers payments, money transfers, lending, savings, investments and insurance products. The company had 41.5 million monthly active users in the three-month period that ended on Jun 30, or nearly 56 per cent of the Philippines' adult population, according to its prospectus. GCash users completed payment transactions worth 9.84 trillion pesos in the first half of 2026. BIGGEST IN THE PHILIPPINES Mynt's IPO surpassed Monde Nissin's 52.2-billion-peso IPO in 2021 to become the largest-ever IPO in the Philippines, according to data compiled by LSEG. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said the listing came at a time when the stock market needed renewed investor interest and broader participation, adding that attracting fresh capital remained a challenge. He said strong demand from local and international investors offered a "reason for optimism" and reflected continued confidence in Filipino enterprises. The Mynt IPO attracted more than 20 cornerstone investors, who committed about US$500 million, or nearly 60 per cent of the base deal, according to the company. Investors included BlackRock, Citadel, Fidelity International and the International Finance Corp. Mynt sold 8.03 billion shares at 6.60 pesos each. The exercise of an overallotment option increased the deal size to 60.9 billion pesos from 53 billion pesos. Mynt plans to use the proceeds to fund growth in its digital financial services business, product development and general corporate purposes, according to its prospectus. Mynt said that for the six-month period that ended on Jun 30, its net income rose 7.3 per cent from a year earlier to 10.82 billion pesos. Revenue rose 10.4 per cent to 43.27 billion pesos.

item.title: Gold eases as higher oil prices stoke inflation concerns
item.description: Gold edged lower on Tuesday as rising oil prices stoked inflation concerns, with investors looking to next week's Federal Reserve meeting for clues on the US interest-rate outlook.
item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: Gold edged lower on Tuesday as rising oil prices stoked inflation concerns, with investors looking to next week's Federal Reserve meeting for clues on the US interest-rate outlook. Spot gold fell 0.5% to $4,120.49 per ounce by 0909 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.5% to $4,139.10 per ounce. "Persistent inflationary pressures, driven by high energy prices, continue to support expectations of further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve," said Ricardo Evangelista, ActivTrades director and CEO. Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. "The Fed is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged in October, so the main focus will be on its guidance regarding a possible increase in December," Evangelista added. Recent comments from [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"Fed"] officials signalling little [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"urgency"] for further policy tightening have tempered expectations of a rate hike at the central bank's October 27-28 policy meeting, but traders see a 90% chance of a hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Although gold is traditionally considered an inflation hedge, higher rates dent its appeal as investors prefer yield-bearing assets. The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, due next week is also on investors' radar for clues on the interest-rate outlook. Elsewhere in Japan, central bank Governor Kazuo Ueda [USN:L1N465004 TEXT:"said"] underlying inflation was "quite close" to the 2% target, signalling scope for further rate hikes. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.2% to $57.1931 per ounce, platinum fell 0.1% to $1,639.45 per ounce and palladium dropped 0.9% to $1,110.06 per ounce.

item.title: 原油先物下落、対ロ制裁免除を見極め 中東の供給懸念続く
item.description:
Anjana Anil
[２０日 ロイター] - アジア時間の原油先物は下落。市場は、ロシアのエネルギー輸出に絡む一部...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
原油先物下落、対ロ制裁免除を見極め　中東の供給懸念続く 10:31 配信

米テキサス州ミッドランド郊外で稼働する石油ポンプジャック。2025年6月、米テキサス州ミッドランドで撮影。REUTERS/Eli Hartman

Anjana Anil

[２０日 ロイター] - アジア時間の原油先物は下落。市場は、ロシアのエネルギー輸出に絡む一部の制裁と関税を免除する米大統領令の影響を見極めている。一方、サウジアラビアとイエメンでの攻撃を受け、中東からの供給が混乱するとの懸念がくすぶっている。

００１０ＧＭＴ（日本時間午前９時１０分）時点で、北海ブレント先物は０．４９ドル（０．４５％）安の１バレル＝１０９．０６ドル。２０日に期日を迎える米ＷＴＩ先物１１月限は０．３３％安の１０３．３２ドル。取引の中心となっている１２月限は０．４６ドル（０．４７％）安の９８．０８ドルとなっている。

北海ブレント先物は前営業日に一時１１０．７０ドルまで上昇し、５月２０日以来の高値を付けた。

トランプ大統領が１６日夜に発令した大統領令は、ロシア製品への関税や同国産の石油・ガスの購入に対する制裁措置など、米国の主要な対ロ制裁と関税を免除する内容。ただ、トランプ氏は１７日、この問題について最終決定はまだ発表していないと述べた。ルビオ米国務長官は、政府当局者が状況を評価するためにさらなる時間が必要だと語った。

国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）が先週発表したデータによると、ロシアの９月の原油生産量は日量６万５０００バレル増の８４３万バレルとなったが、前年同月を約８７万バレル下回った。

ＫＣＭトレードのチーフアナリスト、ティム・ウォーターラー氏は「ロシアからのディーゼル燃料供給が増える見通しは、理論上は需給逼迫の緩和につながるものの、トレーダーは湾岸地域のエネルギーインフラへの被害がさらに広がるリスクをはるかに重視しているようだ」と述べた。

イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は１９日、サウジアラビアのエネルギー施設や空港、軍事施設に対して複数の攻撃を実施したと発表した。対象にはサウジ西部の紅海沿岸都市ヤンブーにある国有石油企業サウジアラムコの施設、シャイバ油田、首都リヤドのキング・ハリド国際空港、アブハ空港が含まれるという。サウジ当局は直ちにこの主張を確認しておらず、ロイターも独自に確認できなかった。

また、イエメンのシャブワ州では１９日、暫定政府治安部隊の訓練施設がフーシ派の攻撃を受け、５８人が死亡、２００人以上が負傷した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：石油価格、イラン攻撃による急騰から持久戦へ コラム：ホルムズ封鎖で石油貿易に変化、米州が最大の受益者に アングル：世界の石油備蓄、イラン戦争長期化による大規模供給途絶を乗り切れるか 焦点：エジプト沖ドローン攻撃が脅かす原油輸送代替ルート、スエズ運河巡る安全性に懸念 アングル：原油価格、イラン紛争でも予想ほど急騰しなかった訳 最終更新: 10/20(火) 10:31 ロイター

FAST

Oct 20 : Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. Brent crude futures climbed 52 cents, or 0.47 per cent, to $110.07 a barrel by 0628 GMT, after rising as high as $110.70 a barrel in the previous session to their highest since May 20. The US West Texas Intermediate crude (WTI) contract for November delivery, set to expire on Tuesday, was up 0.36 per cent to $104.03. The more-active December contract rose 26 cents, or 0.26 per cent, to $98.80. "Oil prices remain well-supported ... This suggests the market is pricing in a significant risk premium, given the situation's volatility," ING analysts said in a note on Tuesday.

"However, if flows continue uninhibited despite the geopolitical environment, the risk premium would likely erode slowly. Clearly, there are no signs of this yet." At least 18 vessels were reportedly attacked over two weeks, which keeps the risk premium intact, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday. HOUTHIS CLAIM ATTACKS ON SAUDI FACILITIES Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they launched several attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, such as an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and Abha airport. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims and Reuters could not independently verify them. Also on Monday, a Houthi attack on a training camp for government security forces in Yemen's Shabwa province killed 58 people with more than 200 injured. The renewed attacks heightened fears about regional stability and underscored continuing risks to energy supply from the region, keeping oil prices above $100 a barrel. In the US, crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last week along with product inventories, a preliminary Reuters poll showed on Monday. Friday's executive order by President Donald Trump waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs, including goods duties and penalties for purchases of its energy. However, Trump said on Saturday he had yet to announce a final decision on the matter, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials wanted more time to evaluate the situation. Russia's crude oil production increased by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million bpd, but remained about 870,000 bpd below that of a year ago, the International Energy Agency said last week.  "While the prospect of additional Russian diesel supply offers some theoretical relief, traders appear far more focused on the ongoing risk of further damage to energy infrastructure across the Gulf region," said Tim Waterer, KCM Trade chief analyst.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month
item.description: Nuclear talks between the US, China and Russia could happen as soon as next month after Donald Trump says he is open to a three-way summit.

Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month

Nuclear talks between the US, China and Russia could happen as soon as next month after Donald Trump says he is open to a three-way summit.

Traditional Russian wooden dolls depicting China's President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin are displayed for sale at a souvenir shop in St Petersburg, Russia on Nov 21, 2024. (File photo: AP/Dmitri Lovetsky)

FAST

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday (Oct 19) he is open to three-way arms-control talks with the leaders of China and Russia as soon as next month, raising the prospect of an unprecedented meeting and a major diplomatic gambit for the US president. "We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearisation," Trump told reporters outside the White House. "If President Xi wants to have it, I'd have it. I'm sure we'd talk about other things like trade too." Trump has tried to thaw frosty relations with Beijing and Moscow as those non-Western powers grow closer. A three-way meeting would also raise alarm from Europe to Asia over private deals that weaken Washington's transatlantic and Indo-Pacific alliances. But a deal struck between the three countries could also lower global tensions. An end to Russia's war in Ukraine could resolve the biggest threat in decades to European security, and a deal on arms would bind the three nations with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons.

In recent days, Trump has moved to warm ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin, announcing a diesel-fuel deal and signing an order on Friday waiving key sanctions on Moscow . Trump has also sought stable relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who in turn has nurtured close ties with Putin. So far, Trump has not delivered on a campaign promise to quickly end the war in Ukraine. The White House has been discussing for weeks a possible meeting between the leaders focused on denuclearisation on the sidelines of the Nov 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, according to a person familiar with the matter. Putin later pitched using such a meeting to negotiate an end to the four-year-old Ukraine conflict in a manner that would favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the discussions. Putin's suggestion came during an Oct 9 phone call with Trump that yielded the deal on Russian diesel. Earlier on Monday, the Kremlin said that the potential meeting had come up in talks. The three leaders have met separately but never held formal talks together. The White House did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Russian and Chinese embassies in Washington also did not reply to requests for comment. Trump's diesel deal with Putin and the executive order waiving sanctions on Moscow have drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , who has warned they would embolden Putin and prolong the war. Speaking about the possible meeting on Monday, Trump said, "I would do it, not so much for Ukraine because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine." He added that "Zelenskiy is not helping matters much," and that "it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine." Moscow launched one of its broadest air assaults in months overnight, cutting power to more than half a million households and damaging energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Ten people were reported killed.

Related:

Commentary: Why do Trump and Xi keep meeting if the hard issues remain unresolved?

US and China discuss reciprocal visits to nuclear sites: Reports

TRUMP SEEKS NUCLEAR TALKS Last week, Trump told reporters he thought a denuclearisation deal with Russia and China was possible, but that it "doesn't have to be this year." It's not clear how advanced any talks between the countries are. Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty expired earlier this year. The New START treaty, signed in 2010, allowed a single extension, which Putin and former US President Joe Biden agreed to for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty. China's foreign ministry said last week that its "nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia" and that it would be "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage." Trump has already agreed to attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen next month, marking his second trip to China this year and his third visit with Xi over the same period. China, Russia and the United States are all members of APEC. On Monday, Trump downplayed the idea of another high-profile meeting in China, with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. "I get along with him very well, and I'm not sure that anybody's asking for a meeting," he said. Trump previously said he planned to meet with Kim this year. North Korea has publicly indicated that it is not open to talks aimed at convincing Pyongyang to give up its nuclear weapons.

item.title: Australian lawmaker loses leg after vehicle attack being probed by anti-terror police
item.description: Doctors have amputated the leg of an Australian lawmaker after a man rammed her with his car and then reversed to hit her a second time, local media and officials said on Tuesday, in an incident being investigated by anti-terrorism police.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose
item.content:encoded: Doctors have amputated the leg of an Australian lawmaker after a man rammed her with his car and then reversed to hit her a second time, local media and officials said on Tuesday, in an incident being investigated by anti-terrorism police. Helen Haines, an independent, underwent surgery overnight and remained in critical condition after Monday's attack in the small rural town of Wangaratta, north of Melbourne. The motive for the attack has yet to be revealed, but Australia’s prime minister has linked it to a climate of ugly, polarised political debate in the country. "It's clear that there was a deliberate act here. This wasn't an accident, someone just skidding off the road," Albanese told ABC News. Early investigations suggested the car hit Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, he said. Australian media, citing unidentified sources, reported Haines had lost one leg as a result of her injuries and that doctors were working to save the other leg. A 43-year-old man was arrested following the attack, with counter-terrorism authorities among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. Police are considering potential charges, including causing harm to a public official - an offence that carries a maximum penalty of 10 years' imprisonment - as they work to establish a motive for the attack. "At this stage it appears this is an isolated incident," Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett said. STRUCK TWO TIMES Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told ABC Radio that witnesses said the alleged attacker reversed the vehicle and struck Haines a second time before a bystander intervened. Ricky Jefferies ran from his barber shop, restraining the attacker and removing a knife from him after initially believing the incident was a car accident, Australian media reported. "I heard a loud bang with no brakes. It was crazy, I just ran out to the front to see what's happening," Jefferies told reporters outside his shop. "I didn't realise the seriousness of the situation initially, and once it became relevant I just did what I could and what others were already trying to do." 'TURN TEMPERATURE DOWN' Violent attacks on politicians are extremely rare in Australia, where federal lawmakers, state leaders and even prime ministers are regularly seen in supermarkets and coffee shops, attending community events and chatting with voters with minimal security. [USN:L4N4650NF TEXT:"Haines"] worked in nursing and midwifery and as an academic before being elected to parliament as an independent in 2019 in the seat of Indi. She retained the seat in 2022 and 2025. Outside the hospital where Haines is being treated, Melbourne resident Shawn Hill said the attack showed that "the political climate is becoming more and more polarising today." "No one deserves to be put at risk of anything, especially someone who is serving the people and trying to do what is best for the Australian community," Hill told Reuters. Albanese urged Australians to engage more respectfully with one another, expressing concern about growing division in the country. He also noted a "significant increase" in threats against politicians in recent years. "We all have a responsibility to turn the temperature down," Albanese said. "I really don't want to see the character of Australia change."

Pakistan’s army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir is due to visit Tehran on Tuesday, according to a Pakistani official and Iranian media.

Pakistan has played a key mediating role between the U.S. and Iran this year.

The scheduled visit follows earlier talks between Munir and Iranian leaders in the summer that focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an expedited termination of the conflict.

item.title: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
item.description: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to a record low.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to a record low as Americans worried about high gasoline prices and appeared ready to punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections , according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday. Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed. Asked which party they would vote for if the congressional elections were held today in what is known as a "generic ballot" question, some 47% of registered voters in the nationwide poll picked Democrats and 35% chose Republicans. The 12-point Democratic advantage was the widest over the current election cycle and could bolster Democratic hopes of seizing control of the US House of Representatives and the US Senate. For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his term. Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents want to see in charge in Congress. While these polls provide a view of national public sentiment, they do not capture all the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House, contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages. A Reuters/Ipsos poll two weeks earlier showed Democrats leading Republicans by 7 points, 44% to 37%. Much of the drop in support for Republican congressional candidates was due to a larger share of women saying they would pick Democrats. Some 50% of female voters said they would vote Democratic, compared to 32% eyeing Republican candidates. Men also favored Democrats, but by a smaller margin. Trump's popularity has suffered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel. The war triggered a surge in gasoline prices, hitting household finances. Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the economy, including 37% of self-identified Republicans. Voters in the poll picked Democrats over Republicans as the better stewards of the economy, by 40% to 33%. The survey, which was conducted online, gathered responses from 1,679 US adults, including 1,279 registered voters. The poll's results had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for all respondents and 3 points for registered voters.

item.title: Residents winched from rooftops as torrential rain hits eastern Spain
item.description: Helicopters rescued people stranded on rooftops as torrential rains swept across eastern Spain on Monday, as floods and storms killed at least three people and shelter-in-place orders remained in force for more than 80,000 residents.
item.dc:creator: Eva Mañez
item.content:encoded: Helicopters rescued people stranded on rooftops as torrential rains swept across eastern Spain on Monday, as floods and storms killed at least three people and shelter-in-place orders remained in force for more than 80,000 residents. The downpour from Storm Adam cut off several towns along the Mediterranean coast as rivers burst their banks and streets turned into torrents, leaving scenes reminiscent of the [USN:L8N3W10M6 TEXT:"catastrophic flooding"] that killed more than 230 people in the Valencia region two years ago. Members of the Military Emergencies Unit found the body of a woman in the town of Oliva during rescue operations on Monday, bringing the death toll to three, regional broadcaster A Punt reported, citing sources from the unit. Two other women were confirmed dead over the weekend: one whose body was washed up on a beach in Sagunto, in the eastern region of Valencia, and another who was [USN:L8N464012 TEXT:"swept away by floodwaters"] in Cabrera de Mar, near Barcelona. 'IT'S A DISASTER' In Els Poblets, northeast of Alicante, cars and vans were piled on top of one another from the force of the water as residents tried to salvage what they could from their homes. “The village, well, it's a disaster. Some people have lost everything all over again, just like in 2007, when exactly the same thing happened," chef Javier Fornez, 49, said. Meteorologists say human-driven climate change makes such [USN:L8N3M628P TEXT:"extreme weather events"] more frequent and destructive. National weather agency AEMET said torrential rains linked to Storm Adam dumped exceptional amounts of rain across eastern Spain, with Pego, in Alicante province, recording 632 mm (25 inches) in 36 hours, while several locations in southern Valencia and northern Alicante exceeded 500 mm over the same period. AEMET issued several red alerts, warning local people to avoid all travel and to seek higher ground. On Monday morning, 800,000 residents were under shelter-in-place orders, but that had been reduced to 87,000 in eight municipalities by late afternoon. HEAVY-DUTY VEHICLES STRUGGLE TO ACCESS SOME AREAS More than 2,000 people were evacuated, mainly in Oliva, and authorities carried out nearly 100 rescues in Valencia and Alicante, the Civil Guard police said. The mayor of Pego, Enrique Moll, told A Punt radio that several people were still waiting to be evacuated by helicopter from their roofs. All access routes to the town were blocked and even heavy-duty military vehicles were unable to move forward in some areas, he added. The deputy mayor of the coastal town of Oliva, Salvador Llopis, told state broadcaster TVE on Monday that emergency services were rescuing trapped residents, particularly elderly people stuck inside their homes with water up to their waists. "They have to stay on top of tables and furniture to avoid getting wet," he said, adding that the rains had started to ease after causing extensive damage to infrastructure. More than 100,000 students in Valencia region have had classes suspended due to the alerts, while the central government has deployed emergency units from the military and national police. The focus of the storm was expected to shift to Catalonia on Monday afternoon, especially Barcelona and Girona provinces, where more than 100 mm of rain could fall in less than 12 hours. Authorities warned that the risk was heightened because the soil was already saturated from previous storms.

item.title: Bruce Campbell’s Top Picks for Oct. 19, 2026
item.description: Gran Tierra Energy (GTE) is a Calgary-based energy producer with a catalyst of transforming through the proposed sale of its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses. Closing would leave it debt-free, with ...
item.content:encoded:
Bruce Campbell, President & Portfolio Manager, StoneCastle Investment Management Focus: Canadian Stocks

Top Picks: Gran Tierra , Aecon , Eli Lilly MARKET OUTLOOK: Our early warning indicators triggered a couple of weeks ago, prompting us to pay closer attention to beadth changes under the market’s surface. These signals have appeared three other times in the past five years, with each occurrence followed by increased market volatility. Last week’s rotation reinforced that caution. Investors rewarded defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples, with utilities also showing renewed strength, while moving away from higher-beta areas. We have not shifted to a full out defensive portfolio stance, but we have begun reducing beta and positioning for lower volatility. The signals warrant preparation; they do not, on their own, justify a wholesale retreat from equities. We see the first quarter of 2027 as a potential period of greater vulnerability, particularly if economic activity begins to weaken. We’re watching for confirmation and adjusting our exposure as conditions evolve. How to set BNN Bloomberg as your preferred source on Google Market-moving news, fast:  Get the BNN Bloomberg App now Sign up for the Market Call Top Picks newsletter at  bnnbloomberg.ca/newsletters TOP PICKS: Bruce Campbell's Top Picks: Gran Tierra, Aecon & Eli Lilly Bruce Campbell, president & portfolio manager at StoneCastle Investment Management, shares his top stock picks to watch in the market.

Gran Tierra (GTE TSX) Gran Tierra Energy (GTE) is a Calgary-based energy producer with a catalyst of transforming through the proposed sale of its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses. Closing would leave it debt-free, with approximately $354 million in cash plus $92 million receivable, supporting growth and potential buybacks. We see meaningful upside from Alberta’s Clearwater area and applying modern exploration and drilling techniques in Azerbaijan. Shareholders have approved the sale; regulatory approvals and regular closing conditions remain; closing is targeted for late December to early January. Aecon (ARE TSX) Aecon Group (ARE) is one of Canada’s leading construction and infrastructure companies. Management’s multi-year turnaround centres on shifting away from fix price contracts to contracts that better support more predictable profitability. The improvement is showing: second-quarter adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) doubled, while backlog stood at $10.5 billion, providing substantial visibility into future work. Canada’s infrastructure investment provides a further tailwind, particularly in nuclear power, utilities, transit and defence. Recent awards include Aecon’s $1.7 billion share of an Alberta power project supporting data centres. We see improving margins and infrastructure demand supporting continued earnings growth, although legacy project claims remain a risk. Eli Lilly (LLY TSX) A global pharmaceutical company developing treatments for diabetes, obesity, cancer and other serious diseases. Its key growth drivers are Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity. Lilly fits our move toward larger companies with less economically sensitive demand, while maintaining strong earnings growth potential. It raised full-year guidance following both its first- and second-quarter results, with second-quarter revenue increasing 48 per cent, primarily driven by Mounjaro and Zepbound. We believe long-term healthcare demand offers greater resilience if economic activity slows. We are using LLY- TSX in this case with the Canadian Depositary Receipt (CDR) trading on the Canadian exchange. item.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada
item.description: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the US.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Stephenson, Maria Cheng
item.content:encoded: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on [USN:L6N3Z2101 TEXT:"separation"], in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a [USN:SPN44J009 TEXT:"trade war"] with the US. CBC News, Canada's government-funded national broadcaster, called the result late Monday after 33% of the vote had been counted. At the time of the call, 76% of tallied votes were in support of the "remain" side versus 23% in favor of the province moving forward with a binding vote on separation. The [USN:L6N46019J TEXT:"referendum"] was nonbinding. "Albertans made a clear choice," Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement. "They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other." "Canada is greater than the sum of its parts," he said. Pollsters and analysts had repeatedly dismissed the possibility of a separatist victory, citing data that showed about one-third of residents in the western province supported a future referendum on leaving. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced the referendum in May, saying it was “time to have a vote, understand the will of Albertans on this subject, and move on.” Late Monday, Smith issued a statement on social media saying she was "very pleased" that early results show widespread support for remaining in Canada. She said she would address Albertans on Tuesday to discuss the results and "where our province goes from here." A small but vocal group of separatists has campaigned for months for an independent Alberta, arguing that the province’s energy wealth is subsidizing poorer parts of Canada and that Alberta would be far richer without Ottawa bureaucracy impeding its path. Last week, Carney told a rally in Calgary that voting to leave Canada would be “a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep division,” and appealed to Albertans to “vote like Canada depends on it.” Carney, who grew up mostly in Alberta, acknowledged that Albertans have often felt slighted by Ottawa and said his government had approved a proposed [USN:L1N45N0PP TEXT:"new pipeline"], adding that Alberta is critical to helping Canada reduce its dependence on the US. Alberta's referendum follows two previous referendums on separation in the majority French-speaking province of Quebec. Quebecers voted to stay in Canada in both instances. First Nations groups have also [USN:L6N41R10Y TEXT:"objected"] to the idea of an independent Alberta, as their land treaties with Ottawa predate the province’s creation within Canada. CBC News reported strong turnout from First Nations. One southern Alberta polling station in an area that is home to the Siksika Nation temporarily ran out of ballots, and then stayed open until after 10 p.m. MT (0400 GMT) to ensure everyone in line had the chance to vote. Still, Monday’s referendum is unlikely to end the separatist movement in Alberta. Before the referendum, some separatist leaders said they would continue to pursue another vote even if most Albertans voted to remain. According to data released on October 16 by the pollster Angus Reid, 62% of Albertans believe “there will never be an end to the separatist movement” in the province. Alberta's referendum also included [USN:L6N3ZF146 TEXT:"nine other nonbinding questions"] on topics including immigration, access to provincial services — such as education, social care and healthcare — and voter identification requirements. Results for those questions were still trickling in.
